results.content: One of the most important aspects of financial modeling is to make realistic and consistent assumptions about the costs of the business or project. Cost assumptions are the estimates of the future costs that will affect the performance and profitability of a project, business, or investment. - **historical data**: Historical data refers to the past cost information of a similar project, business, or investment, that can be used as a reference or a starting point for making cost assumptions. - ****industry benchmarks****: Industry benchmarks refer to the average or standard cost information of a group of similar or comparable projects, businesses, or investments, that can be used as a guide or a benchmark for making cost assumptions. - **sensitivity analysis**: Sensitivity analysis refers to the process of testing and evaluating the impact of different cost assumptions on the outcome and results of a financial model, by changing one or more cost variables and observing the changes in the key performance indicators, such as net present value, internal rate of return, or payback period. One of the most important aspects of financial modeling is to validate and update the cost assumptions that underlie the projections and scenarios.
